title: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Citigroup and BGC

Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights Citigroup and BGC
Zacks Equity Research

BGC
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 24, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses Citigroup, Inc. C and BGC Group, Inc. BGC.

Industry: Investment Banking

Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/3033666/2-investment-bank-stocks-to-buy-as-industry-tailwinds-strengthen

While persistent inflation, elevated borrowing costs and the Federal Reserve's cautious monetary policy stance could temper dealmaking, the Zacks Investment Bank industry is expected to benefit from resilient economic growth and robust corporate investment, supporting mergers and acquisitions (M&As) and underwriting activities. Geopolitical tensions, trade uncertainties and market volatility are likely to sustain trading revenues and client engagement. 

Rising investments in artificial intelligence (AI), technology and digital platforms may elevate near-term expenses but are expected to improve operational efficiency and long-term profitability. So, industry players like Citigroup, Inc. and BGC Group, Inc. are worth betting on.

Industry Description

The Zacks Investment Bank industry consists of firms that provide financial products and services, including advisory-based financial transactions to corporations, governments and financial institutions worldwide. These started as partnership firms focused on initial public offerings (IPOs), secondary equity offerings, brokerage and mergers and acquisitions (M&As). 

Gradually, the companies have evolved into providers of various other services, including securities research, proprietary trading and investment management. Industry players work mainly through three product segments: investment banking (M&As, advisory services and securities underwriting), asset management and trading and principal investments (proprietary and brokerage trading).

Themes Shaping the Future of the Investment Bank Industry

Underwriting and Advisory Businesses Momentum to Persist: Following a prolonged slowdown since 2022, investment banking activity has regained momentum, supported by the Trump administration's pro-business agenda, deregulation efforts and improving corporate confidence. Strategic restructuring, private equity transactions and consolidation are driving M&A activity, while favorable market conditions are supporting a selective IPO recovery. A resilient economy, AI-related investments and healthy transaction pipelines should support advisory and capital-markets revenues. 

However, the recent U.S. midterm election results have introduced fresh policy uncertainty, with potential legislative gridlock and increased regulatory oversight that could affect dealmaking and underwriting activities. Additionally, geopolitical tensions, tariff uncertainties, elevated borrowing costs and cautious investor sentiment could delay deal execution and temper the pace of recovery. Despite these challenges, sustained corporate investment and financing requirements are expected to support investment banking revenue growth.

"Global equity positioning became increasingly bearish last week, with new short positioning emerging as the dominant flow across most major indices," Citi wrote in a new note.

The U.S. is said to have seen the largest adjustment, led by aggressive short additions in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, as investors reacted to weakening AI sentiment and higher rate expectations.

Citi said the shift was driven mainly by outright new shorts, rather than investors exiting existing long positions.

Despite the sell-off, the bank said positioning in large-cap indices remains only moderately bearish. Risk is instead concentrated in the small-cap Russell 2000, where "extremely elevated and profitable short exposure leaves the index vulnerable to an outsized short-covering rally."

In Europe, the bank said weakness was concentrated in the EuroStoxx, where investors both opened new shorts and sold existing long positions, while DAX positioning eased back into net short territory.

Citi flagged that a sizable base of loss-making legacy long positions in the EuroStoxx could trigger capitulation flows if market weakness persists.

Asia remains the focal point of bearish sentiment, with positioning in South Korea's KOSPI and Hong Kong's Hang Seng again nearing extended levels.

"Importantly, positioning risks are becoming increasingly asymmetric across regions," Citi said, adding that concentrated and profitable short books remain the key vulnerability in Asia.

Image from Pixabay

After the 2008 financial crisis, Washington decided that some banks were too big to fail. Between Nov 12 and Nov 23, the White House showed it holds the same view about at least one person. He is Jensen Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of Nvidia.

On Nov 12, Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as chief executive. The board later said the reason was personal behavior at odds with its code of conduct. His exit came weeks after reports that US intelligence suspected a woman close to him of working for China. She is a former executive of a Singapore cloud computing firm. That day, the President suggested Apple's Tim Cook take over. On Nov 17, the board's new chair said it did not intend to bring Huang back.

On Friday, Nov 20, President Trump said he would like to see Huang "make a big apology and go back." On Monday, Nov 23, Nvidia announced that the board had reinstated him. Its filing said this came after "input from senior levels of the United States government." "I made the deal," the President told CNBC.

Investors cheered. Nvidia's stock rose 31.5% on Monday to $165.05, its biggest one-day gain since May 2003. It added about $954 billion of market value in a single session. Some of that was a rebound. Nvidia had fallen 14% on Friday, the day Reuters reported that SEC staff were examining potential accounting issues there. The S&P 500 fund (SPY) also rose 4.7% on Monday. Even beyond the market's move, Nvidia gained about $810 billion that day. Measured from Thursday's close, before Friday's report, the gain beyond the market was about $430 billion.

Nvidia swung from a 14% fall on Friday to a 31.5% gain on Monday. If you are waiting for a calmer moment to buy, your cash can earn something while you wait. title: Is Earnings Rebound Altering The Investment Case For Citigroup (C)?

Is Earnings Rebound Altering The Investment Case For Citigroup (C)?
Sasha Jovanovic

C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup has recently raised multiple tranches of fixed rate senior unsecured notes across maturities from 2028 to 2056, while also making leadership hires in equity capital markets and U.S. retail branches, and hosting a Taiwan Corporate Day that highlights its global services reach.

The mix of fresh bond funding, regional leadership changes, and deepening institutional engagement points to Citigroup focusing on balance sheet flexibility, capital markets execution and cross border client flows rather than headline trading activity.

We will look at how this combination of fresh bond issuance and executive reshaping fits into Citigroup's broader investment narrative.

Compare how Citigroup's funding and leadership reshuffle stacks up against other large financial institutions by scanning a curated set of list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (23 results)

Citigroup Investment Narrative Recap

To own Citigroup, you need to believe the bank can keep turning its global Services, U.S. cards and wealth engines into steady returns while keeping risk under tight control. The analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St expects services growth, AI driven efficiency and business simplification to support double digit returns on tangible equity. The latest bond funding and leadership moves look incremental rather than thesis changing for that view.

The most important near term swing factor remains execution on restructuring, capital return and the January Banamex and broader capital plans, while the biggest risk is still regulatory and conduct setbacks that could eat into those returns. Recent news does not materially change either the main catalyst or the key vulnerability.

The fresh run of fixed income offerings, including the US$30.325 million 6.05% notes due 2031 and US$59.367 million 6.00% notes due 2031, is the clearest operational link to the funding narrative. These senior unsecured, mostly callable issues extend Citigroup's maturity ladder and support the balance sheet that underpins the services led growth story.

For you as a shareholder, the relevance is practical rather than dramatic. Stable term funding helps Citigroup keep supporting cross border payments, securities services and U.S. cards while it pursues AI driven cost efficiencies and prepares for capital redeployment from Banamex. The risk side is that higher coupon debt raises interest expense, so execution on productivity and fee income needs to keep pace.

Citigroup's current narrative ties a forecast revenue level of US$108.8b and earnings of US$22.4b by 2029 to an assumed 9.3% yearly rise in revenue and an earnings increase of about US$4.5b from the US$17.9b earned today.

Citi slashed its price target on Salesforce (CRM) stock by nearly 25% on Monday, after checks with the company's customers and partners pointed to sluggish demand for its core software.

Analyst Tyler Radke trimmed his target to $198 and kept a "Neutral" rating on Salesforce. His revised estimate still signals a potential upside of nearly 10% from its previous close.

Citi's research note adds pressure on Salesforce shares, which are already down roughly 30% from their high in early September.

www.barchart.com
What's Behind Citi's Warning on Salesforce Stock

One Salesforce partner told Citi that the firm's sales pipeline had weakened meaningfully as rivals won business and customers signed shorter contracts.

Radke's broader checks also pointed to hesitation among clients to commit to larger deals.

That matters for Salesforce heading into the fourth quarter because shorter contracts bring renewal decisions forward, giving competitors another chance to win accounts sooner.

They can also make future revenue harder to predict, even when a customer keeps paying the same annual rate.

For investors reading the December report, the fourth-quarter outlook may say more about that pressure than the headline earnings figure, which covers a quarter that has already ended.

Salesforce Earnings: What to Expect

Radke's checks found improving momentum for Agentforce and Data 360, but demand was uneven and relatively few customers had put AI agents into live use.

That distinction is significant for Salesforce shares.

A customer testing an agent on a narrow task can generate early demand — while a rollout across a support operation can drive recurring usage and spending.

Consensus estimates for CRM are $2.41 per share of earnings (EPS) for fiscal Q3, representing about a 9.4% year-over-year decline.

On the flip side, however, Salesforce pays a dividend yield of 0.95%, which makes it somewhat more attractive as a long-term holding.

Wall Street's Consensus Rating on Salesforce

It's worth mentioning that other Wall Street analysts do not currently agree with Radke's call.

The consensus rating on Salesforce remains Moderate Buy, with a mean price target of about $286, indicating significant upside potential from current levels.

detail:

A $4.3 Billion Fund Just Bought These 3 Stocks ©maxkabakov from Getty Images, AndreyPopov from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Prana Capital Management, which manages $4.31 billion, made Nasdaq, Citigroup and Charles Schwab its three biggest new or added positions in the third quarter, its 13F shows.

It added 417% to its Citigroup shares, more than doubled its Nasdaq stake and opened a new position in Schwab.

Since Sept. 30, Nasdaq is up 12%, while Citigroup is down 15% and Schwab is down 8%.

The numbers back Schwab best: record third-quarter earnings, about 12x forward earnings and 29% upside to analysts' average target.

The third-quarter 13F deadline has passed, and one $4.3 billion fund put its new money into financials. Prana Capital Management's 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed Nov. 16, shows its three biggest new or added positions were Nasdaq (NDAQ:NASDAQ), Citigroup (C:NYSE) and Charles Schwab (SCHW:NYSE).

Prana manages $4.31 billion in all, and its 13F lists $3.11 billion of US stocks in 122 positions. Each of the three is 2.4% to 2.8% of its 13F stocks, so none is a huge bet on its own.

Nasdaq has already run

Prana more than doubled its Nasdaq stake in the quarter, to 957,241 shares worth $88 million at Sept. 30. That made it the fund's No. 7 holding, at 2.8% of its 13F stocks, and it also held put options on Nasdaq with a notional value of $4 million. Since Sept. 30, the stock is up 12%.

The business has earned it. Nasdaq's third-quarter net revenue rose 13% to $1.5 billion, its Solutions revenue grew 17% to $1.2 billion, and it won 8 of the 10 largest operating company IPOs of the quarter. And General Motors moved its stock listing to Nasdaq from the NYSE in late October.

Analysts have raised their sights all year. Their average target has climbed from $104 a year ago to $115, its high for the year:

Nasdaq (NDAQ): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

That target is only 12% above the last close, and at about 22x forward earnings, Nasdaq is the priciest of the three.

TIKR tracks 18 analysts on Nasdaq. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Nasdaq, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Nasdaq's Analyst Ratings

Citigroup is the biggest add

Prana raised its Citigroup share count 417% in the quarter, to 640,638 shares worth $83 million at Sept. 30. That's its No. 8 holding, at 2.7% of its 13F stocks. The stock is down 15% since then.

Citi's third-quarter GAAP net income rose to $5.2 billion from $3.8 billion a year earlier, and its return on tangible common equity hit 12.6% over the first nine months of 2026. Analysts expect EPS of $11.40 this year and $13.06 in 2027, and both estimates have risen over the past three months. Still, management expects a fourth-quarter return in the high single digits, with Markets revenue falling about 20% or more from the third quarter.
